en.p: As shown in the figure, there is a hyperbola $C:\ \dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ with foci $\mathrm{F}(4,\,0)$ and $\mathrm{F'}(-4,\,0)$. Let $\mathrm{P}$ be the point in the first quadrant where the parabola with focus $\mathrm{F}$ and directrix the $y$-axis meets hyperbola $C$. If $\mathrm{H}$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $\mathrm{P}$ to the $y$-axis, then $\overline{\mathrm{PH}}:\overline{\mathrm{HF}}=3:2\sqrt{2}$. Find the value of $a^{2}\times b^{2}$. (Given that $a>b>0$.) [4 points]
